items.article: Maya Jama, Michael Sheen and Bella Ramsey are among this year's celebrities taking part in the show. The Celebrity Traitors is back for a second series, and viewers will see the likes of Michael Sheen, Jerry Hall, Richard E Grant and Amol Rajan at the round table along with Bella Ramsey, Leigh-Anne Pinnock, Maya Jama and King Kenny. There are 21 celebrities taking part in total - two more than last year - and there will be an extra episode after the huge popularity of last year's series. The extended 75-minute debut episode starts at 20:00 BST on Thursday, with Claudia Winkleman again hosting the murderous game. Viewers can expect some fresh ideas, and executive producer Sarah Fay said they "always want to push the envelope" with the show's elaborate tasks. "We're always trying to evolve existing ideas to bring them into a new life or coming up with different cultural references," she told the show's press launch. The celebrities will be playing for a £100,000 cash prize for charity.

If the weapon of the attack on Captain Machchhar by his Omani co-pilot, was indeed an axe, it might not have passed through security at all because commercial aircraft carry a crash axe or similar tool to breach hard surfaces (like a plane's fuselage) as emergency equipment. items.text: 1st look at Zoo Atlanta's new giant panda
items.article: The zoo shared a new video and update on how Fu Shuang and Ping Ping are settling in after arriving from China. Zoo Atlanta is giving panda fans a new look at one of its newest arrivals. The zoo released a new video of female giant panda Fu Shuang on Wednesday, just days after she and male giant panda Ping Ping arrived in Atlanta from China over the weekend. In its first update on the pair since their arrival, Zoo Atlanta said both pandas are settling into their new home and have exceeded the animal care team's expectations as they acclimate. "Both Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are eating well and adjusting more and more each day," the zoo said. The pandas are not yet visible to visitors as they undergo a routine quarantine period, which is expected to last around a month. Zoo Atlanta said it will announce at a later date when the public will be able to meet them. Ping Ping and Fu Shuang arrived at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on Sunday, Sept. 27, aboard a FedEx "Panda Express" Boeing 777.

Kate looked sensational in a flowing gown by Jenny Packham, in regal purple. But her choice of jewellery was also telling. A dazzling, heart-shaped amethyst sautoir necklace once owned by Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother and the famous Collingwood pearl earrings that belonged to Diana , Princess of Wales, honoured the memory of two remarkable women who represented the royal family before her. items.text: Discover how Nestlé is made by Britain
items.article: After joining Nestlé for a brief work placement over three decades ago, Richard Hastings now works to drive the company’s future distribution plans When you go into the supermarket for your favourite Nestlé products, you probably don’t give much thought as to how those items got there. But the same can’t be said for Richard Hastings. As the head of logistics for Nestlé UK and Ireland, it’s the responsibility of Richard and his team to make sure that shop shelves across the UK are stocked with all the Nestlé essentials – from Shreddies and KitKat to Nescafé Gold Blend and Dolce Gusto pods. Richard’s Nestlé career began in 1990, with a work placement as part of his degree in supply chain and logistics. “It was meant to be just 12 months, but I think I did nearly 16 in the end,” he says, explaining that he was immediately thrown in at the deep end. “And within two weeks of joining, I was sent to work in Scotland for six months!” After graduation, Richard worked for his dad for a bit before setting off to see the world – but it wasn’t long before Nestlé came calling with an offer he couldn’t refuse. “I was in Penang when I got a fax from my parents saying I’d received a letter from Nestlé,” he explains.

items.article: Premier League clubs are waiting to learn what punishment will come Manchester City's way after a verdict was reached on their 115 charges While we might finally have a ruling on Manchester City's 115 charges, a punishment could still be some way away. The eight-time Premier League champions have been found guilty of breaches of financial rules in relation to the 2009-18 period, though they were cleared of one charge in relation to non-cooperation with the investigation. City continue to protest their innocence, saying they are "disappointed and surprised" by the findings . However, while there could be further twists and turns, repercussions could follow sooner rather than later. A number of potential punishments have been floated, ranging from points deductions and transfer bans to instant relegations. However, one football fan has gone directly to the subject of what might happen to City's squad members. They called for "An NFL style draft where 1 by 1, each of the other 19 Premier League teams get to select one of their players to sign free of charge." JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page You're probably wondering how this would all pan out. Well, in true NFL style, the teams at the bottom get first pick and those at the top have to wait their turn, in the interests of levelling the playing field.

His actions reflect the courage, responsibility and spirit of service that strengthen our nation.” “In moments that test us, standing together and standing with the nation matters. At EaseMyTrip, we believe that when one of our own stands strong for the nation, we must stand with them and their family. items.article: Vintage-inspired mini golf in San Clemente. Mai tais on a sunken ship in Anaheim. Sprawling red rocks in Trabuco Canyon. It’s time to go deeper into great, big, always juicy O.C. With California’s coast getting pounded by strong waves amid a strengthening El Niño, residents and city leaders are turning to big rocks and seawalls to protect homes and keep railroads from falling into the sea. Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison can proclaim victory after settling a lawsuit with state attorneys general that held up his company’s merger with Warner Bros. But Ellison will have considerable work ahead to repair frayed relations with Hollywood talent. L.A. Times 2026 Gold Award honoree Norm Langer has kept the deli his parents opened in 1947 a welcoming place for all of Los Angeles. Oh, and it serves the nation’s finest pastrami, according to the late Jonathan Gold and many others. Columnist Mirjam Swanson writes USC coach Lincoln Riley’s embarrassing lack of leadership cost the Trojans a potential win over Oregon. Presley Gerber’s death has brought much mourning as well as questions about how he could have overdosed on drugs while inside the luxury residence.

items.article: While it may sound dull, getting to know your credit score can be a simple way to gain a better understanding of your finances. Are you the kind of person who knows when your bills get paid, the cost of your weekly shop, and the exact number of days until payday? If so, you’re already keeping a close eye on your money. But there’s one item on your money to-do list that can easily slip under the radar: checking your credit score. Credit scores can feel technical at first, but checking yours can be a useful way to understand your credit profile. You don’t need to be an expert to take that first look. With ClearScore, you can access your credit score and report for free, alongside handy personalised insights. And if you sign up by September 30 , you’ll be entered into a prize draw for the chance to win £5,000! So what exactly is a credit score, why does it matter, and what can it tell you?
